    Who are we?

    We’re innovators, collaborators, and above all, Team Credo. For more than a decade, we’ve pushed technology forward. Our story isn’t about where we’ve been. It’s proof that believing in opportunity gives us the courage to keep breaking barriers ahead.

    Credo’s Benefits and Perks

    Purpose, people, and possibilities guide our employee experience.

    Purpose

    We invest in what matters. From meaningful-future shaping projects to competitive compensation, we empower you to grow your career while making a lasting impact. We offer:

    • High-value compensation and equity packages to help you fuel your purpose outside of work too.
    • Global health and wellbeing plans for all employees and their families with higher-than-industry employer contributions for non-statutory benefits.
    • Professional development assistance to help you broaden your knowledge and stay current with developments in your field.

    People

    Connection starts within. We collaborate, celebrate wins, and create an environment where everyone can do their best work. We offer:

    • Inclusive and equitable workplace standards that are reflected in both our policies and our day-to-day experiences.
    • Flexible time to recharge from paid vacations, holidays, and parental leave (up to 16-weeks in the US and statutory leave globally) plus options for other extended absences.
    • On-site amenities at most office locations, from fitness centers and lactation rooms to meal options and celebrations that bring our people, their friends, and their families together.

    Possibilities

    Our belief shapes what’s next. Credo’s technology powers the most reliable and energy-efficient connections around the world – and our team powers new products and markets that come next. We offer:

    • The opportunity to shape the future of connectivity by enabling infrastructures that will underlie the next wave of AI/compute systems.
    • Meaningful social responsibility with Credo Cares where you can lend your skills and create positive change in communities around the world.
    • Global connections that expand your professional network as you collaborate across cultures to drive innovation.

    Our Core Values

    Keep learning.
    Keep innovating.

    We believe curiosity fuels progress. We embrace change, think critically, and push technology – and ourselves – forward.

    Own the start.
    Own the finish.

    We believe in doing what we say we’ll do. We take challenges head-on, solve with integrity, and learn from every outcome.

    Stay humble.
    Stay focused.

    We believe in building with purpose, not ego. We let data guide us, results define us, and progress speak for itself.

    Lead with connection.
    Lead with care.

    We believe collaboration, respect, and fun is how great work gets done. When we operate across departments, time zones, and diverse ideas, then we operate as Team Credo.

    Credo Cares represents our commitment to community

    At Credo, we believe that innovation and social responsibility go hand in hand. That’s why we launched Credo Cares — an initiative to bridge the gap between the resources of the tech industry and the needs of charitable organizations.

    Senior Design Verification Engineer

    Architecture & Firmware

    Pittsburgh Office

    		 Apply Now

    About the role

    Team Credo is seeking a hands-on verification engineer to contribute to digital design verification for our high-performance networking and interface IP portfolio. In this role, you will help architect scalable, reusable verification environments, support UVM testbench development, contribute to verification plans and coverage goals, and partner closely with design and architecture teams to deliver high-quality, production-ready silicon.
      
    Base salary range is $92,000- $154,000 a year. The base salary offer will depend on factors such as education, experience, training, skills, qualifications, and location. This position is also eligible for a discretionary bonus, equity and a full range of medical and other benefits.
     
    Why Credo
    • Purpose: We invest in what matters. From meaningful-future shaping projects to competitive compensation, we empower you to grow your career while making a lasting impact. 
    • People: Connection starts within. We collaborate, celebrate wins, and create an environment where everyone can do their best work.
    • Possibilities: Our belief shapes what’s next. Our technology powers the most reliable and energy-efficient connections around the world – and our team powers new products and markets that come next.

    Responsibilities

    • Define end-to-end verification strategy and architect reusable, scalable UVM-based testbench frameworks for IP and subsystem-level verification.
    • Translate architecture and functional specifications into comprehensive verification plans, test scenarios, checkers, assertions, and coverage models.
    • Lead the development of reusable UVM verification components including agents, drivers, monitors, scoreboards, reference models, and constrained-random stimulus.
    • Own regression planning and execution, failure triage, debug, root-cause analysis, and verification sign-off criteria.
    • Drive functional and code coverage closure, identify verification gaps, and improve methodology for quality and efficiency.
    • Partner closely with design, architecture, firmware, emulation, and post-silicon teams to ensure robust verification of complex data-path and protocol-centric designs.
    • Review microarchitecture for testability and observability, and influence design decisions that improve verification effectiveness and debug productivity.
    • Develop automation and scripting infrastructure to improve regressions, reporting, stimulus generation, and verification productivity.
    • Lead design and verification reviews, establish best practices, and mentor engineers on methodology, coding quality, and debug techniques.
    • Support critical product and field issues requiring deep insight into architecture, RTL behavior, and verification environment behavior.
    • Ensure compliance with relevant standards, as well as internal and external specifications.
    • Evaluate AI-driven verification techniques and streamline existing methodologies around AI-enhanced solutions.

    Qualifications

    Basic Qualifications
    Seven or more years of relevant experience and a strong track record in the following areas:
    • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical and/or computer engineering.
    • Technical leadership in ASIC/SoC verification methodology and execution.
    • Strong understanding of digital design concepts including state machines, data paths, FIFOs, clock-domain crossings, resets, low-power behavior, and performance-sensitive architectures.
    • Expertise in SystemVerilog, UVM, constrained-random verification, assertion-based verification, and development of synthesizable and behavioral models where appropriate with emphasis on configurability and reuse.
    • Strong automation and scripting skills in Python, Perl, Tcl, and shell for regressions, reporting, stimulus, and workflow optimization.
    • Advanced debugging skills across RTL, testbench, waveforms, assertions, and regression failures.
    • Networking protocols, specifically 802.3 (Ethernet), PCIe, CXL, and related standards.
    • On-chip bus and interconnect protocols including AMBA: CHI, AXI, APB, etc.
    • Forward Error Correction (FEC) algorithms.
    • Experience with at least one of these major tool suite: Cadence, Mentor, and Synopsys tools for simulation, lint, and synthesis.
    • Knowledge of AI workloads a plus.

    Principal AI System Architect

    Digital Design Engineering

    San Jose Office

    		 Apply Now

    About the role

    Credo is looking for a Principal AI System Architect to join our team in San Jose, CA, reporting to AVP, XPU system AI interface. This role needs to solve the system-level interconnection challenges that connect XPUs (NPU/GPU/custom silicon) into working AI infrastructure. This role needs to follow and define how compute elements are wired, networked, and orchestrated together at node, rack, and cluster scale so that large-scale LLM training and inference run efficiently across the platform. We strongly prefer candidates with a hands-on NPU hardware background and real experience taking NPU silicon into production deployment at scale.
     
    Base salary range is $220,000 – $280,000 a year. The base salary offer will depend on factors such as education, experience, training, skills, qualifications, and location. This position is also eligible for a discretionary bonus, equity and a full range of medical and other benefits.
     
    Why Credo
    • Purpose: We invest in what matters. From meaningful-future shaping projects to competitive compensation, we empower you to grow your career while making a lasting impact.
    • People: Connection starts within. We collaborate, celebrate wins, and create an environment where everyone can do their best work.
    • Possibilities: Our belief shapes what’s next. Our technology powers the most reliable and energy-efficient connections around the world – and our team powers new products and markets that come next.

    Responsibilities

    • Define the memory and interconnection architecture linking XPUs to memory and across node, rack, and cluster boundaries -not the internal design of the NPUs/GPUs/CPUs themselves.
    • Solve communication and topology bottlenecks that arise from all kinds of parallelism strategies during distributed LLM training and inference.
    • Define how XPUs utilizes the memory and interconnect fabric, ensuring workloads map cleanly onto the network topology.
    • Work with silicon, memory, networking, and software teams to specify interconnect fabric requirements and resolve integration issues between compute nodes.
    • Bring hands-on NPU hardware architecture judgment to interconnect and system design decisions, informed by direct experience taking NPU silicon from definition through bring-up, validation, and production deployment.
    • Track leading open LLM architectures to anticipate how model structure will stress interconnect and system topology.
    • Lead and mentor a team of architects focused on system interconnection; represent this strategy to leadership and partners.

    Qualifications

    Basic Qualifications
    • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or related field required
    • Ten years in XPU or AI interconnect system design, architecture and micro architecture working experience.
    • Five cycles of complete ASIC tapeouts.
    • Strong foundational understanding of computer architecture, including GPU, NPU, and/or CPU design principles; deep, hands-on NPU hardware architecture expertise.
    • Familiarity with large language model architectures and distributed training/inference concepts (e.g., parallelism strategies, model serving) through coursework, research, or personal projects.
    • Demonstrated analytical ability, for example, through published research, thesis work, or quantitative project work- with a track record of independently studying and synthesizing technical material.

    DustPhotonics, now part of Credo, is a leading developer and manufacturer of silicon photonics solutions enabling the next generation of AI and cloud infrastructure. This role owns the critical front-end processes of our semiconductor supply chain, coordinating day-to-day execution across external silicon FABs, wafer-level testing facilities, and dicing vendors.     • Wafer-Level Testing Scheduling: Coordinate logistics and capacity planning for optical and electrical wafer-level testing (WLT), ensuring timely availability of test and yield data.

    • Supply Chain Interface: Serve as the primary operational contact for silicon foundries, testing facilities, and other relevant manufacturing vendors.

    • Prepare and review indirect tax filings (VAT/GST/Sales & Use Tax, property tax etc.) across applicable jurisdictions, ensuring timely and accurate reporting in compliance with local regulatory requirements, and reconcile indirect tax accounts
    • Manage and monitor inter-company (I/C) transactions and settlements across entities, ensuring balances are accurately recorded and reconciled in line with transfer pricing policies
    • Perform transfer pricing (TP) calculations and true-up analyses in accordance with intercompany agreements and TP policy; assist in preparing transfer pricing documentation and supporting schedules
    • Coordinate corporate income tax return preparation with external tax vendors, including managing the information requests, reviewing vendor-prepared returns and workpapers for accuracy, and tracking filing deadlines across relevant jurisdictions
    • Prepare and file FBAR (Foreign Bank Account Report) and other foreign asset/account reporting requirements in compliance with applicable regulations
    • Support quarterly and annual income tax provision calculations under ASC 740 and other applicable accounting standards 
    • Assist in responding to tax authority information requests and audit queries, and prepare supporting documentation and analysis for audit defense
    • Support special tax studies and analyses such as R&D tax credit studies, Section 382 ownership change/NOL limitation analyses, and other ad hoc technical projects as needed with a strong willingness to learn and take on new areas of tax responsibility as they arise
    • Manage relationships with third-party tax advisors and vendors, including coordinating deliverables, reviewing work product, managing timelines and budgets, and acting as the primary point of contact for outsourced tax work
    • Identify and implement opportunities to leverage AI tools and automation to improve the efficiency and accuracy of tax processes, workpapers, and reporting
    • Partner with FP&A, Accounting, Legal, and Treasury teams, and work closely with regional/global tax colleagues across different jurisdictions 

    Qualifications

    Basic Qualifications
    • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, Finance, Taxation, or related field (CPA, CA, or equivalent professional qualification preferred)
    • 3-5 years of relevant tax experience; a combination of public accounting and corporate in-house tax experience preferred
    • Hands-on experience with tax compliance, transfer pricing, intercompany settlements, income tax provision
    • Demonstrated ability to manage third-party service providers, including scoping work, reviewing deliverables, and managing budgets/timelines
    • Strong Excel skills; along with familiarity NetSuite is preferred
    • Comfort leveraging AI tools and technology to streamline tax processes and improve efficiency
    • Excellent analytical, organizational, and communication skills
    • Ability to work effectively with cross-functional and cross-border/global teams
    • Self-starter with a strong willingness to learn and take on new tax projects and areas of responsibility
    • High attention to detail and ability to manage multiple deadlines in a fast-paced environment

    Senior Infrastructure Engineer

    Information Technology

    Modiin Office

    About the role

    We are seeking a Senior Infrastructure Engineer to own the operation, reliability, security, and continuous improvement of our global server infrastructure. The role is primarily focused on physical and virtual servers, operating systems, storage, backup, identity, monitoring, automation, and cloud compute, while providing broad Tier 2–3 troubleshooting across systems, networking, and security. The engineer will resolve complex incidents, lead infrastructure projects, and partner with network, security, cloud, development, and operational teams to deliver scalable, compliant, and cost-effective services.
      
    Why Credo 
    • Purpose: We invest in what matters. From meaningful-future shaping projects to competitive compensation, we empower you to grow your career while making a lasting impact.
    • People: Connection starts within. We collaborate, celebrate wins, and create an environment where everyone can do their best work.
    • Possibilities: Our belief shapes what’s next. Our technology powers the most reliable and energy-efficient connections around the world – and our team powers new products and markets that come next.

    Responsibilities

    • Server and Systems Operations: Own Tier 2–3 administration and support for Linux and Windows servers, virtualization, cloud compute, storage, backup, identity, patching, configuration, capacity, and lifecycle management across global environments.
    • Reliability, Monitoring, and Automation: Monitor server and platform health, analyze performance and availability, resolve complex incidents and root causes, automate provisioning and recurring operations, and implement improvements that reduce risk and downtime.
    • Infrastructure Security: Harden servers, remediate vulnerabilities, maintain privileged access and security baselines, support audits and compliance controls, and coordinate incident response with cybersecurity teams.
    • Network and Cross-Platform Support: Provide Tier 2–3 troubleshooting for DNS, DHCP, TCP/IP, routing, switching, firewalls, VPNs, load balancing, and application connectivity as they affect server and infrastructure services.
    • Projects, Recovery, and Governance: Lead server migrations, upgrades, infrastructure deployments, disaster-recovery testing, documentation, standards, change management, vendor coordination, and operational handoff for global services.

    Qualifications

    Basic Qualifications
    • Five or more years of experience in infrastructure or systems engineering with substantial hands-on Tier 2–3 responsibility for enterprise server operations, complex incident resolution, and production support.
    • Strong administration skills across Linux and Windows Server, VMware or comparable virtualization, cloud compute, SAN/NAS storage, backup and recovery, Active Directory or IPA, and performance monitoring.
    • Working knowledge of DNS, DHCP, TCP/IP, routing, switching, firewalls, VPNs, segmentation, identity, access control, system hardening, vulnerability management, and security incident support.
    • Experience with PowerShell, Bash, Python, Ansible, or comparable tools, plus ITSM, change, patch, asset, monitoring, and configuration-management processes.
    • Proven ability to diagnose cross-platform issues, perform root-cause analysis, lead infrastructure projects, develop technical documentation, and coordinate effectively with global network, security, cloud, and application teams.
       
    Preferred Qualifications
    • Red Hat, Microsoft, VMware, or equivalent enterprise infrastructure certification.
    • Experience with high-availability clustering, enterprise backup, disaster recovery, storage integration, patch orchestration, and server lifecycle management.
    • Proficiency with configuration management, infrastructure automation, scripting, and enterprise workload scheduling such as LSF or an equivalent platform.
    • Hands-on experience operating secure server workloads and associated network services in AWS, Azure, or GCP.
    • Experience supporting semiconductor, EDA, high-performance computing, or similarly demanding Linux-based engineering environments.

    About the role

    As a Lab Technician in this role, you’ll partner with product engineers to validate eval boards and SLT programs, collecting data across temperatures using the Cobra, thermal machines, or automated handlers. Working with the team, you’ll document test results, log performance metrics, and report anomalies or failures according to procedure, and help run automated handlers for engineering and pre-production testing on customer samples. The team will also work with you on calibrating, cleaning, maintaining, and performing basic repairs on testing stations and handlers.
      
    Base pay range is $20.19 – $37.50 an hour. The base pay offer will depend on factors such as education, experience, training, skills, qualifications, and location. This position is also eligible for a discretionary bonus, equity and a full range of medical and other benefits.
     
    Why Credo
    • Purpose: We invest in what matters. From meaningful-future shaping projects to competitive compensation, we empower you to grow your career while making a lasting impact.

    Responsibilities

    • Build bench setups, verify and transfer to the handler. 
    • Install relevant software on laptops used on our bench and handler setups.
    • Hand test or handler run for silicon characterization, correlation, program buyoff and customer sampling.
    • Perform basic test related debugging and preventative maintenance.
    • Support NPI planner on shipments to customers.
    • Support T/PE’s engineering work.

    Qualifications

    • Associate degree in Electronics Engineering Technology, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical discipline (or equivalent military/disaster electronics training).
    • One or more years of experience working on a semiconductor test floor or in an electronics manufacturing environment.
    • Hands-on experience with handlers, oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies and basic hand tools.
    • Familiar with windows environment and proficient with Microsoft tools like Word, Excel, Outlook, or Teams to log test data, write reports and collaborate.
